requirement:
When loading a supported legacy evidence record that did not capture its
procedure version, Habeas represents that missing version as `*`.
In-place conversion preserves this wildcard rather than assigning the current
version. The wildcard matches any
requested review revision under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records.procedure_match`.
The record is current when its recorded inputs and all existing application
freshness checks still match. Version matching leaves the subject, reference-set,
input, determination, citation, and site checks intact.

For new assessments, Habeas's validation value supplies a concrete review revision
other than `*`, and the assessment records it.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate. They cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_conversion.legacy_freshness`. I did not request any implementation source.

**Legacy loading represents the missing version as `*`**
- `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[legacy_conversion_preserves_every_historical_field_without_resolving_sources]` decodes legacy records for definition, citation and site subjects. It asserts `record.revision == "*"`.
- `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once]` loads legacy records for all four review kinds through `load_evidence`. It asserts `loaded.revision == "*"`.

**In-place conversion preserves `*` instead of assigning the current version**
- The same `evidence_format` test asserts `native["review_version"] == "*"` after `encode`, and checks the round trip with `view(&native) == old`.
- `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[current_legacy_authoring_converts_without_configuration_and_stdout_never_converts]` runs the real `author_evidence_with_options` on a legacy file. It asserts the rewritten file has `review_version == "*"` and still views as the old record.
- The multi-kind test also asserts `native["review_version"] == "*"` for each mutated legacy record.

**`*` matches any requested review revision**
- `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[native_freshness_checks_versions_inputs_and_application_fields]` asserts a `*` record is current against `"future-review-version"`. It also asserts a concrete `old-concrete-version` record is not current against `REVIEW_VERSION`. That second assertion shows the wildcard is what makes the difference.
- It also asserts `"any"` is used for a stale `*` record, which shows the wildcard does not hide stale inputs.

**The record is current when inputs and application checks match**
- The multi-kind test checks that unmodified legacy records produce no findings. It also checks that native `*` records and native `REVIEW_VERSION` records produce identical findings.

**Version matching leaves the other checks intact**
- The multi-kind test mutates each historical field on a `*` record and requires a specific finding, identical to the legacy-format finding. The mutations cover:
  - determination false;
  - a stale input hash or text;
  - changed subject text;
  - a changed reference set;
  - citation file, item and commentary;
  - site requirement, file, item, queries, fixmes and `applies=false`.
- Staleness is separated from loading errors: such records still load, and format errors do not.

**New assessments use a concrete revision other than `*` and record it**
- `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[authoring_keeps_the_prepared_subject_snapshot_and_concrete_version]` asserts `value["review_version"] == REVIEW_VERSION` and that it is not `"*"`. It also decodes the record and checks that it is not current after the source changed.

I found no untested obligation or boundary the text names. The cited `procedure_match` rules are context only, and the tests also exercise them (an exact, non-wildcard mismatch is not current).

The revision matches when the stored `Record::revision` is `*` or equals the
requested revision exactly. Only the complete stored value `*` is a wildcard;
other values compare literally. A wildcard leaves dependency comparison and
result decoding unchanged. It matches revisions for the selected source and
criterion only, and does not supply evidence for other criteria.
